diagnosis.note: The HTTP 401 was expected for a non-HTML request without a browser session and was not treated as the startup failure.

assessment: The R113 native-footer DOM insertion correlated with sustained Web CPU and AppView reconnect churn.
The immediate Web-only rollback reduced observed Web CPU and restored fresh document and protected status requests.
This bounded observation is sufficient to reject R113 as the active release, but it does not isolate one browser-side mutation as the sole cause.
residual_risks: R112 restores the independent lower-left launcher, so the requested native sidebar integration is not active.
A browser tab holding the pre-restart WebSocket and session must open a new document after rollback.
A future native integration must avoid inserting persistent nodes into the upstream React-owned footer subtree and must include a runtime CPU/reconnect acceptance gate.
No real model request or account switch was sent. Switching starts a new backend session and does not resume or replay semantic output.
